content:
Online media outlet "Hu·Shuo Lou Shi" (胡‧說樓市) reported on Friday (2nd) that a detached house valued over HK$100 million at One Stanley in Stanley has steel reinforcement quality issues. Analysis of the steel rebar quantity in certain positions showed a shortfall of approximately 41% to 75% compared to the approved plans. The Buildings Department stated on Saturday (3rd) that it had received a complaint and, after inspection, found that the protective layer of a ground floor beam was not fitted with steel wire mesh as required by the plans, and that the steel reinforcement configuration in some floor slabs did not match the plans. According to "Hu·Shuo Lou Shi", the developer,建灝地產 (K&K Property), had issued a lawyer's letter requesting the suspension and cessation of the related reports, stating that "if unverified allegations affect project sales, we reserve the right to pursue legal liability." The vendor of One Stanley, Kinway Limited, issued a statement last night saying it takes the incident very seriously and will follow up rigorously. If any mistakes are found after investigation, it will carry out remedial work for the affected property in accordance with the law, while pursuing the responsibility of the relevant parties.

Developer: K&K Property (建灝地產)　Contractor: Hoi Yuet Construction (海悅建築)

No. 128 Wong Ma Kok Road, Stanley, is a low-density luxury project. The entire development has only 82 units, including 32 detached houses and 11 apartment blocks. The developer is K&K Property (建灝地產), and the contractor is Hoi Yuet Construction Engineering (海悅建築工程), a subsidiary under China State Construction Engineering (Hong Kong) (中國建築興業). K&K Property was established in 2013 by Law Ka-kui (羅家駒) and his son Law Kin-yat (羅建一), who are descendants of the Bossini family.

"Hu·Shuo Lou Shi" followed the incident for over half a year. The report stated that the property owner purchased the unit in April 2024, and during renovation in August last year, discovered abnormalities in the surface concrete of some floor slabs. The plaster surface layer below the floor of the second-floor master bedroom was peeling off, and subsequently the steel rebars were found to be "out of position" with inconsistent spacing.

The report stated that after the Buildings Department conducted scanning and removal inspections, the registered structural engineer commissioned by the owner analysed the data from the Buildings Department. The analysis showed that the number of main steel rebars in some positions of the second-floor study was approximately 41% to 75% less than the approved plans; and in some positions of the first-floor bedroom ceiling, the shortfall was approximately 42% to 57.9%.

The Buildings Department issued an "Occupation Permit" in July 2023

In response to the "Hu·Shuo Lou Shi" report, the Buildings Department stated that it has been following up the investigation seriously after receiving the complaint. The Department pointed out that the detached house was issued an "Occupation Permit" in July 2023, and the owner carried out renovation after purchasing it. The Buildings Department received a complaint from the owner's representative in January this year, stating that there were safety issues with the floor slab structure inside the house. After an on-site inspection in March, it was considered that the overall building structure did not show obvious danger. The Department has written to require the project's registered structural engineer to submit relevant material test reports and certificates.

Buildings Department: Steel reinforcement configuration in some floor slabs does not match plans

The Buildings Department stated that during the period from June to September this year, it conducted multiple on-site inspections, including concrete strength rebound hammer tests, surface thickness gauge surveys, surface radar surveys of steel reinforcement configuration, core-drilling compressive tests, and on-site opening-up inspections, among other work, and is currently analysing the relevant data. The Buildings Department stated that the test and inspection results found that the protective layer of a ground floor beam of the detached house was not fitted with steel wire mesh as required by the plans; in addition, the steel reinforcement configuration in some floor slabs did not match the plans.

Written to developer and others requesting assistance in investigation

The Buildings Department stated that the above situation "does not constitute obvious danger" and will conduct further investigation. The Department has written to the project's developer, contractor, authorised person and registered structural engineer, requesting assistance from all parties in the investigation. The Buildings Department also reminded the industry that, in accordance with the Buildings Ordinance (《建築物條例》), building professionals and contractors must supervise and carry out construction in accordance with the approved plans. The Department also stated that if it is found after investigation that any building professionals and contractors have violated the Buildings Ordinance, it will definitely follow up rigorously, including prosecution and/or the initiation of disciplinary action.

Vendor: Will give an account at an appropriate time after gathering and verifying more information

Kinway Limited, the vendor of One Stanley, responded that the company takes the incident very seriously and will follow up rigorously. The company stated that, according to the information released by the Buildings Department, the Department considers that the overall building structure of the property does not show obvious danger. Kinway stated that it is currently gaining a detailed understanding of and verifying the incident, will fully cooperate with the Buildings Department's investigation, and will give an account to the public at an appropriate time after gathering and verifying more information. If any party is found to have committed mistakes in construction quality or other related matters after investigation, it will carry out remedial work for the affected property in accordance with laws and regulations, and pursue the responsibility of the relevant parties in accordance with the law.
